qa_pairs.question: How can users request full H100 GPUs for their compute jobs on the Nibi cluster using Slurm options?
qa_pairs.answer: To request full H100 GPUs on the Nibi cluster, users can use various Slurm options. For a single H100-80gb GPU, use `--gpus=h100:1` or `--gpus=h100_80gb:1`. To request multiple H100-80gb GPUs per node, options include `--gpus-per-node=h100:2`, `--gpus-per-node=h100:3`, or `--gpus-per-node=h100:4`. For multiple full H100 GPUs spread anywhere across the cluster, use `--gpus=h100:n`, replacing 'n' with the desired number of GPUs.

qa_pairs.question: What are the available Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) configurations for H100 GPUs on the Nibi cluster, and how does one request a specific MIG instance for a compute job?
qa_pairs.answer: Approximately half of the GPU nodes on the Nibi cluster are configured with Multi-Instance GPU (MIG) technology, offering three instance sizes. These include H100-1g.10gb (1/8th of the computing power with 10GB GPU memory), H100-2g.20gb (2/8th of the computing power with 20GB GPU memory), and H100-3g.40gb (3/8th of the computing power with 40GB GPU memory). To request one of these specific MIG instances for a compute job, users should use the corresponding Slurm option: `--gpus=h100_1g.10gb:1`, `--gpus=h100_2g.20gb:1`, or `--gpus=h100_3g.40gb:1`.

qa_pairs.question: How can users access the Nibi cluster through a web browser, and what functionalities does this method provide?
qa_pairs.answer: Users can access the Nibi cluster via a web browser using Open OnDemand (OOD) by navigating to https://ondemand.sharcnet.ca/ and signing in with multifactor authentication. This web-based platform simplifies cluster access by providing a user-friendly interface that offers options to open a Bash shell terminal or launch a remote desktop environment.
